name: Raghu Dahibara Aloodum
signature_dish: Dahibara aloodum — black-gram bara soaked in light dahi, topped with aloodum, the city's signature breakfast
must_try: dahibara aloodum (plain — no onion, no sev)
why_it_matters: Recognised across Odia media as 'the oldest seller of dahibara in town' — Raghu Bhai's stall at Bidanasi Chowk has been running for generations (he no longer mans the counter himself, his heirs do). The unique pitch: dahibara aloodum served the original way — no onion, no sev, no toppings, just bara in light dahi with the aloodum spooned over. Sells out within hours of opening.
insider_tip: Opens 4pm and frequently sells out by 7. Come at 4-4.30pm for the first hot batch — wait by 6 means you might miss the bara entirely. Stand-and-eat only, no seating. Cash, small notes. The 'plain' version is the move; ignore vendors who upsell toppings.

name: Trinath Sahoo Dahibara Aloodum
signature_dish: Sweet-spicy dahibara aloodum — the modernised Trinath version with sev and chutneys
why_it_matters: 30+ years on Kanika Road in Masik Patna Colony — Trinath was the first dahibara seller in Cuttack to go on online food delivery, expanding the dish's reach beyond the queue. The Trinath style adds sev, chutneys and a sweet-spicy aloodum profile, distinct from Raghu's plain original. Both are correct; locals split the city by preference.
insider_tip: Open earlier and longer than Raghu — easier to time. Pair the dahibara with ghuguni (Bengali-Odia matar curry, dished beside the bara). If you only have time for one dahibara stop, Raghu = original, Trinath = the modern Cuttack default. Zomato delivery works within 6km radius.
signature_address: Kanika Road, Masik Patna Colony, Tulsipur, Cuttack, Odisha 753008

name: Babula Dahibara
signature_dish: Award-winning dahibara aloodum — won India's Best Street Food at Delhi Street Food Festival 2019
why_it_matters: Babula Bhai's Masik Patna Colony stall won India's Best Street Food award at the 2019 Delhi Street Food Festival — the only Odia street food vendor to have taken a national title. Same dahibara aloodum form, but the spice balance is what got him noticed by judges. Sits in the same Masik Patna cluster as Trinath, so easy to do both in one stop.
insider_tip: Evening hours only. Combine with Trinath — they're walking distance and offer different riffs on the same dish. Bring small change; nobody runs UPI here. Sundays the queue is double weekday length.
signature_address: Masik Patna Colony, Tulsipur, Cuttack, Odisha 753008

name: Hotel Akbari Continental
signature_dish: Mutton biryani Cuttack-style — heavier on ghee and whole spices than Hyderabadi
why_it_matters: Established 1985 — reputed as 'the first hotel in Cuttack' to combine sit-down dining, AC and banquet space under one roof. The Dolamundai address (opposite Jagannath Temple) sits inside the old Cuttack Muslim quarter and Akbari's mughlai-Cuttack biryani became the city's reference for celebration meals. 60 rooms, 4.1/5 across 1,800+ reviews. Where wedding parties book the banquet hall.
insider_tip: The biryani is the order — kalia and tandoor are secondary. Avoid the buffet on weekdays; it skews to safer pan-Indian. Banquet hall books up Saturdays — call ahead if you want dinner during wedding season. Parking in-house.
signature_address: Haripur Road, near Dolamundai Jagannath Temple, Sutahat, Cuttack, Odisha 753001

name: Bikalananda Kar's Rasagola — Salepur
signature_dish: Salepur Rasagola — soft, brown, slightly chewy, the recipe since 1922
why_it_matters: Bikalananda Kar founded 'Kar & Brother' in Salepur in late 1922 — the original 100+ year-old rasagola shop whose recipe is now synonymous with Odisha's GI-tagged sweet (granted July 2019). The Government of Odisha co-founded the B. K. Industrial Training Centre in Cuttack with Jadavpur University in his name to train confectioners in 500+ traditional Odia sweets — among the highest honours given to an Indian sweet maker.
insider_tip: The Salepur original is 40km from Cuttack on the Salepur road — a 1-hour detour if you have time. Otherwise the Buxi Bazaar branch in Cuttack and Saheed Nagar Bhubaneswar carry the same Salepur batch daily. The 'special cham cham' (₹295/box) is the under-rated second pick after the rasagola.
signature_address: Main Road, Salepur, Cuttack district, Odisha 754202

name: Ishwara Dahibara Aloodum
signature_dish: Sweet (meetha) dahibara aloodum — Ishwara was the first to add the meetha bara variant
why_it_matters: Located near Biju Patnaik Chowk, Ishwara was the first Cuttack vendor to introduce meetha (sweet) bara into the dahibara aloodum format — a riff on the city's signature breakfast that's now common across newer stalls. Among the cluster recognised as 'one of the oldest in the city' by Odisha Television's Dahibara Aloodum Dibasa coverage.
insider_tip: Try the meetha variant alongside the regular plate — same vendor, two profiles, ₹80 for both. Open from morning till evening. Easy walking from Bidanasi (Raghu) if you want to taste the city's full dahibara map in one outing.
signature_address: Near Biju Patnaik Chhak, Cuttack, Odisha 753001

name: Pahala Rasagola Cluster
signature_dish: Pahala rasagola — brown, soft (not spongy), thin-syrup, 24-hour shelf life
why_it_matters: 100+ rasagola shops lining both sides of NH-16 at Pahala — the chhena-sweet capital of Odisha. Legend traces the recipe to a Jagannath Temple priest who taught local milkmen to curdle excess milk; the GI-tagged 'Odisha Rasagola' (granted July 2019) owes its profile to this village. Brown, soft not spongy, thin syrup, 24-hour shelf life.
insider_tip: Pick the busiest shop, not the prettiest signboard — prices and product are identical across the 100+ stalls. Driving Cuttack→Bhubaneswar the cluster sits ~25km south. Buy a dozen (₹120-150); eat same day. Combine with a stop at the Cuttack Chandi temple en route.
signature_address: NH-16, Pahala village, between Bhubaneswar and Cuttack, Odisha 752101
